steps.what: Verify control data, project tolerances and adjustment assumptions
Calculate adjustment diagnostics and compare results with specified tolerances
Assess control quality and determine the need for additional survey data

tasks.design: Configure native adjustment diagnostics in {OTHER}, the geodetic processing system. Retain observation verification and the decision about whether additional data is needed in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated diagnostic preparation can be separate from engineering judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing adjustment tools calculate residuals and uncertainty from explicit assumptions.
tasks.still_hard: Biased control, poor geometry and apparently acceptable but inappropriate results.
tasks.human_edge: Judge fitness for the project's actual tolerances.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated diagnostic handling; the additional-data decision remains human.

evidence.claim: Trimble Business Center performs least-squares adjustment, supports field-blunder correction and generates adjustment reports; it does not replace project fitness judgement.
The proposed active-time split and saving are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is quality assessment, excluding original observation capture and the separate request for more data.

Field staff produce point identifiers, observations, instrument records and timestamps through existing field work. In s1 the surveyor verifies and captures reference system, units, weights, constraints, tolerance version and dataset snapshot; full extraction and checking stays in the 30 percent.
Missing weights or control provenance pauses diagnostics for manual investigation; no free valid-control or additional-survey-needed flag is assumed.
Test native adjustment configuration before custom code; already automatic numerical runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Current diagnostics automation and project tolerance conventions
research_questions: What active diagnostic handling can be removed after full assumption verification?

steps.what: Verify compiled geodetic data, recipient needs and disclosure conditions
Prepare the geodetic distribution package and metadata manifest
Check content, recipient scope and disclosure and approve the exact package
Distribute the approved package and record delivery status

tasks.design: Configure package export and approved-version delivery in {OTHER}, the geospatial distribution system. The surveyor verifies scope and approves an exact package and recipient set before transmission; delivery failures return to staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated packaging and sending are separate from release decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exports and delivery rules can use a version-bound manifest.
tasks.still_hard: Disclosure limits, coordinate-system meaning and mistaken recipients.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what may be released and whether the recipient will understand its limits.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive packaging and sending; release authority remains with the surveyor.

evidence.claim: PDOK distributes the BRT background map, illustrating geospatial distribution infrastructure without establishing this workflow's saving.
The version-bound package design and savings are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is distribution of already compiled data, excluding original surveying, analysis and compilation.

In s1 the surveyor captures dataset version, requested area, coordinate reference system, format, recipient identity or public release destination, licence, restrictions and required caveats from authoritative sources. All capture and manual rights clarification stays in its 25 percent; unresolved rights stop release.
s2 creates a package and manifest with exact file hashes and destination. s3 supplies approval for those exact fields; any change requires fresh approval. s4 sends only that approved version.
Test native exports and delivery controls before custom code. Failures create a log for the counted additional exception allowance; no automatic alternate-recipient selection.
research_questions: Can approved-version delivery reduce active handling without weakening disclosure checks?

already_counted.description: Scope capture and version-bound release approval

incremental.description: Template checks and delivery exception handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact file hashes, metadata, dataset snapshot, caveats and destination in the approved manifest; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R50 gross50 minus8 upkeep gives net42. Range0-10 allows existing distribution automation or bespoke restricted packages to remove most handling opportunity.

tasks.human_edge: Agree feasible corrective work that addresses the actual error.
tasks.altitude: Request and clarification time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Corrective survey requests require contextual clarification; no generic notification saving is assumed.
